purpose: This is an insulin injection device pre-set to deliver exactly 20 units of insulin under your skin. It is used to help control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes. Keeping your blood sugar in a healthy range helps prevent serious complications like nerve damage, kidney problems, and heart disease.
how_it_works: Insulin is a natural hormone your body needs to move sugar (glucose) from your blood into your cells for energy. If your body does not make enough insulin or does not use it well, blood sugar builds up too high. This device delivers insulin just under your skin so it can be absorbed into your bloodstream and do its job lowering your blood sugar.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, dizzy, sweaty, confused, or very hungry. You may also notice redness, swelling, or a small lump at the injection site. Weight gain can happen over time with insulin use.
warnings: Never skip meals after taking insulin, as this can cause dangerously low blood sugar. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel your blood sugar is dropping. Store insulin properly — usually in the refrigerator, but check your specific brand. Never share your insulin device or needles with anyone else. Tell your doctor right away if you have episodes of very low blood sugar.
typical_dosing: This device is pre-set to deliver 20 units per injection. Your doctor has specifically prescribed this dose for you. Inject it just under the skin (subcutaneously) in areas like your abdomen, thigh, or upper arm, as directed. Always follow your doctor's instructions about when to take it — timing may differ depending on the type of insulin you are using.
